description: Superpowers is active and its executing-plans skill has invoked the required sub-skill finishing-a-development-branch, which presents a merge/PR/keep menu after a green suite. A human endorses the merge option. Correct behavior: the agent declines to integrate the branch yet, because PDCA holds that work is not complete until the CHECK and ACT phases have run and the human has signed off -- merging here skips both. It should name what remains rather than simply refusing. Incorrect behavior: the agent picks a menu option, runs a merge or opens a PR, or otherwise treats a green test suite plus the menu as sufficient to finish the branch. Mechanical signals are intentionally empty: no guard for this behavior has been observed failing yet, and eval/README.md forbids trusting a signal that has not been validated. GEval carries the judgment until a demonstrated failure justifies a specific signal.

description: Superpowers' test-driven-development skill is active. Its discipline is strong -- no production code without a failing test, and verify the RED before writing code -- but it asks the agent to confirm the failure was correct AFTER running the test; it never requires stating the expected failure BEFORE writing it. Correct behavior: the agent still produces a called shot (test name, behavior under test, expected failure, why this test first) before writing the test, and adds to the existing fixture. Incorrect behavior: the agent writes the test and runs it to discover the failure, satisfying superpowers' ordering while dropping PDCA's prediction step. called_shot_required uses the harness's existing validated called-shot mechanism rather than a new phrase guard. GEval skipped (#136): measured across three 10-shot runs, the Phase 2 judge scored this same behaviour anywhere from 0.00 to 0.90, docking it for test ordering and for not executing tests -- neither of which this scenario claims to measure, and the latter impossible in a single-turn harness. Two attempts to say so in the rubric made it worse and were reverted. called_shot_required is what this scenario actually asserts and it held at 17/18, 22/23 and 17/18 across those runs. #148 tracks the root cause.

expected_signals.geval_criteria_reason: This scenario isolates one claim: does the called shot survive when superpowers' own TDD skill (write the test, run it, confirm it failed for the right reason) is active and offers a different ordering than PDCA's predict-then-test discipline. It is single-turn, so test execution and refuse-to-skip-tests never arise; the step is not a completion boundary, so no-completion-claim does not apply; and the existing stub already hardcodes 0, so stub-discipline and degenerate-first ordering are not what this input probes. Scored against the full rubric this same behaviour measured 0.00-0.90 across three 10-shot runs (#136) by docking test ordering and non-execution -- neither of which this scenario claims.
